title: Standardized hypoxia-reoxygenation protocol for Drosophila neurobehavioral assessment
author: Jung, Fehr, et al.

steps.title: Configure hypoxia chamber
steps.instruction: Set the hypoxia chamber to <0.3 % O₂, 29 °C, 50‑70 % humidity and atmospheric pressure. Plan an exposure duration of 2.5 h (or other durations such as 1–6 h as required).

steps.title: Prepare flies for hypoxia and control
steps.instruction: For 1–5 day‑old male Canton‑S flies (20 flies per vial) prepare hypoxia and normoxia groups, keeping CO₂ anesthesia brief and allowing ≥3 min recovery before exposure.

substeps.instruction: Hypoxia group: anesthetize flies with CO₂, transfer all 20 flies into an empty vial **without food**, cover the open side with gauze, and secure the gauze with a rubber band.
Normoxia control: keep flies in their original vials **with food**, anesthetize with CO₂, exchange the plug, cover the open side with gauze and secure with a rubber band.
CRITICAL: Keep CO₂ anesthesia time as short as possible and identical for both groups; ensure all flies have recovered for at least 3 min before hypoxia.

steps.title: Mortality rate analysis
steps.instruction: Calculate mortality for each vial and condition using Excel and fit logistic growth curves in GraphPad Prism.

substeps.instruction: Insert raw data (total flies and dead flies per vial) into a new Excel sheet.
Calculate mortality rate: Mortality % = (Number of dead flies / Total flies in vial) × 100.
Repeat the above for each hypoxia duration individually.
Compute the mean of the three technical replicates for each condition.
Open GraphPad Prism (v8.4.3) and create a new XY table with the four replicate values.
Enter the mean mortality values into the XY table.
Select Analyze → Nonlinear regression (curve fit) → Logistic growth and click OK.
Record the r² value and the fitted equation from the Results sheet.

steps.title: Negative geotaxis analysis
steps.instruction: Adjust negative geotaxis scores for mortality using Excel.

substeps.instruction: Insert the raw mortality data and the raw negative geotaxis data into a new Excel sheet.
Calculate mortality‑adjusted negative geotaxis for each time point: Negative geotaxis % = (Number of flies with intact negative geotaxis / Number of living flies in vial) × 100.

steps.title: Mean activity analysis
steps.instruction: Process DAM monitor files to obtain mean activity per hour, excluding dead flies via a VBA macro.

substeps.instruction: Download the DAMFileScan software from the TriKinetics website.
Select your monitor files (*.txt) and set the analysis period; set bin length to 60 min and ensure all files start at the same time point.
Save the processed files.
Import the saved data into Excel.

Run the following VBA macro to flag dead flies (maximum activity <70 and mean activity <10 after the death point, only if death occurs before the last 24 h):

Sub Exclude_Dead()
    For c = 11 To 42   'columns for the 32 flies after column 10
        For r = 1 To 120   'rows for the 120 h reoxygenation period
            Dim maximum As Integer
            maximum = WorksheetFunction.Max(Range(Cells(r, c), Cells(120, c)))
            Dim mean As Integer
            mean = Application.Average(Range(Cells(r, c), Cells(120, c)))
            If maximum < 70 And mean < 10 And r < 96 Then
                Range(Cells(r, c), Cells(120, c)).Interior.ColorIndex = 3   'mark cells red after death
            End If
        Next r
    Next c
End Sub
Run the macro, then delete all cells that were colored red.
Calculate the mean of each row; Excel will ignore the now‑empty cells, giving a mean activity that excludes dead flies.

steps.title: Sleep cycle analysis (optional)
steps.instruction: Analyze sleep cycles using dedicated software tools.

substeps.instruction: Use SCAMP (Donelson et al., 2012) or ShinyR‑DAM (Cichewicz & Hirsh, 2018) to assess sleep parameters.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for 1–5 days old male Canton-S wild-type flies subjected to 2.5 h of severe hypoxia (< 0.3% O2) at 29°C, 50%–70% humidity and atmospheric pressure, followed by reoxygenation periods of up to 120 h. A hypoxia duration was chosen in this example as it caused a mortality rate of approximately 50% (Figures 4B–4D), thus resulting in a sufficient impact of hypoxia while providing a reasonable number of viable flies for analysis during the reoxygenation period. Besides that, we have also used this protocol for different hypoxia durations (1–6 h), temperatures (e.g., 18°C, 23°C), pressures (e.g., 300 mbar positive pressure) and humidity levels (e.g., 10%–20% humidity) in various male and female Drosophila melanogaster genotypes (e.g., Oregon-R, Trap1+/−, Trap1−/−) of different ages (e.g., 0–1 day old).
